content:
The atmosphere surrounding Meta AI glasses hasn't been great lately. It's so serious that among today's top three paid apps on the US iPhone charts, one is specifically designed to detect who nearby might be wearing smart glasses.

The app's name is anything but subtle: Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner (反朱克伯格智能眼鏡掃描器). It claims to be able to detect when someone nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses and send you an alert.

Enough iPhone users were willing to spend $3 to try this app, pushing it to number 3 on the US iPhone paid App Store charts. It's rare for a new paid app to make it into this ranking.

We haven't tested the app and can't confirm whether it actually works. Even if it does, what you should do after detecting someone wearing AI glasses remains unknown.

Smart glasses equipped with cameras are actually still quite easy to spot, so you probably don't need an app to notice who's wearing them.

Nevertheless, people's attitudes are clear. Enough people are fed up with the concept of AI smart glasses, feeling it involves privacy concerns. If Apple wants to enter the smart glasses market next year, this will be a considerable obstacle.
